lines: Commit → version bump → PR → build → squash-merge → tag → cleanup
Conservative bump default: feat:/fix:/perf: → patch; --bump minor/major to force

card.summary: Full chain: commit → version bump → push → PR → build → squash-merge → refresh main → tag & push → build → cleanup. Halts on any failure.
card.paragraph: The complete close-out for a feature worktree. Two build gates around the merge. A conservative auto version bump (separate chore(release): commit) rides along between commit and push; the matching vX.Y.Z tag is pushed from main after the squash, so the tag always points at a real shipped commit. Designed to be approved as one chain rather than step-by-step.
use_when: Feature branch finished, want one chain to merge & clean up
You want hard build-validation around the merge
You want the version bumped automatically (conservative patch by default; --bump minor/--bump major to force)
dontuse_when: You only need the version bump (no merge) → /stx-version-bump

extras.title: The chain
rows: On main; dirty unrelated; no remote

extras.title: minor / major are explicit-only
extras.html: The auto-policy never picks minor or major on its own — pass --bump minor or --bump major when this PR warrants more than a patch. The one exception is the ! / BREAKING CHANGE: marker, which signals major deliberately.

extras.title: Single chained approval
extras.html: One sentence covers every named step: "Commit these, bump version, push, open a PR, squash-merge, refresh main, tag and push, clean up the worktree." Failures still halt; unexpected files still need a fresh approval. Pass --no-bump to suppress both the bump and the tag, or --no-tag to keep the bump but defer the tag push.
